newsitem.title: USA: Merrill Lynch reports record quarterly profits.
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch reports record quarterly profits.

text.p: Merrill Lynch & Co. said Tuesday its profits rose 14 percent in first-quarter and credited robust market activity for the highest quarterly earnings in the brokerage and investment bank's history.

Merill Lynch reported profits of $465 million, or $2.34 a share, easily beating the consensus Wall Street analyst forecast of $2.07 a share, according to the First Call service, which tracks analyst predictions.
The earnings represented a 14 percent increase from first-quarter 1996 profits of $410 million, or $2.03 a share.

The New York-based company also said its board approved a one-third increase in its quarterly dividend, from 30 cents a share to 40 cents, and a two-for-one stock split, payable May 30 in the form of a stock dividend.
Merrill Lynch's stock jumped $2.75 to $90.50 in consolidated afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange after the announcements.
Net revenues hit a record $3.8 billion, up 18 percent from the year-ago first quarter's $3.3 billion, with increases in all revenue categories, the company said.

"I couldn't be more optimistic about our company's prospects," Chief Executive Officer David Komansky told reporters after the company's annual meeting in Plainsboro, N.J. He also said a correction in the stock market was healthy and re-established a bedrock for stock prices.
Merrill Lynch's rosy earnings report came a day after investment banking firm Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette Inc. reported higher-than-expected first-quarter earnings.

"Our record quarterly earnings were the result of the strength and diversity of our franchise geographically and by market segment, as well as robust market activity that prevailed through much of the quarter, before slowing in March," Chairman Daniel Tully and Komansky said in a joint statement.
Merrill Lynch said total assets in worldwide client accounts reached a record $868 billion at the end of the first quarter, up $137 billion from the year-ago quarter.
Merrill Lynch said it racked up quarterly records in revenues from commissions, principal transactions, investment banking and asset management and portfolio service fees.

Commission revenues totalled $1.1 billion, up 13 percent from first-quarter 1996, while principal transaction revenues -- derived from trades on Merrill's own accounts -- were also $1.1 billion, an 8 percent rise.
Investment banking revenues soared 61 percent to $608 million. Asset management and portfolio service fees increased 20 percent to $646 million.

Merrill said its U.S. and global first-quarter market shares of underwriting of debt and stocks were 16.1 percent and 13.2 percent, respectively, according to Securities Data Co. Securities Data said Merrill had a 19.8 percent market share of worldwide stock and stock-linked offerings in the first quarter.
